messages.author: b02b358f329f98ce
messages.subject: nimble compiler issue
parts:
Hello, I'm having an issue where nimble will not compile basic functions. Here is some example code that will not compile.
```
foo <- nimbleFunction( run = function(x = double(1)) {return(sum(x)); returnType(double())})
cfoo <- compileNimble(foo)
cfoo(1:10)
```
I am using rtools43 and r version 4.3.2 through Rstudio.
The error I get is
```
using C++ compiler: 'G__~1.EXE (GCC) 12.3.0'
Cannot create temporary file in C:\
_files\: Invalid argument
make: *** [C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-43~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf:272: dynamicRegistrations_12_26_13_26_42.o] Error 127
```
My environment PATH from Sys.genenv('PATH') is
```
"C:\\Users\\veron\\anaconda3\\Scripts;C:\\Users\\veron\\anaconda3;C:\\rtools43/x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix/bin;C:\\rtools43/usr/bin;C:\\Program Files\\R\\R-4.3.2\\bin\\x64;C:\\WINDOWS\\system32;C:\\WINDOWS;C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\Wbem;C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\;C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\OpenSSH\\;C:\\Program Files\\Git\\cmd;C:\\Users\\veron\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps;C:\\rtools43\\usr\\bin;C:\\rtools43\\mingw64\\bin;"
```
This seems like a problem where writing to C:\\r_tools\ is not working correctly due to some kind of carridge return getting make from the string. Any help would be appreciated.

parts:
Hmm, I don't know what is going on. I'm not sure what temporary file it is trying to create or why it seems to be trying to use "C:\\Program Files" but then losing "Program" and putting in a carriage 
return. 

A few thoughts:

1) You might look at the other environment variables (`Sys.getenv()`) and see if that gives any clues. 
2) If you run `tempdir()` in R does it reference a standard location for temporary files?
3) Could you try and run a basic Rcpp example to see if this has anything to do with Nimble?

-chris

install.packages("Rcpp")
library("Rcpp")

If this does not work, that would indicate that there is a problem in your R and/or Rtools setup that likely has nothing to do with nimble.

messages.author: 4d8371fa4558c744
messages.subject: Re: nimble compiler issue
parts:
Hi Chris and Perry,

This was very helpful, I've been beating my head against the wall all day with the same error as Veronica but also with a note about Rtools before above the "Cannot create directory error".  
I don't know why this is happening but when I looked at  Sys.getenv(), the BINPREF was set to an old Rtools folder (maybe I did something wrong at installation?). I looked at my other computer where nimble was working fine (using Rtools4.2) and saw it was not listed so I set it using: Sys.setenv(BINPREF=""), now Rcpp and nimble are working.    

I uninstalled previous R versions and Rtools and then installed R4.3.2 and Rtools 4.3.  Just sharing in case this is helpful to others!

Cheers,
Beth

messages.subject: Re: nimble compiler issue
parts:
Hi Chris, Perry, and Beth,

Thank you all for the help trouble shooting this! The issue turned out to be where my temp files were being created. For others who may be experiencing this, my solution was:
```
# change temp file location
write("TMP = 'C:/Users/veron/AppData/Local/Temp'", file=file.path(Sys.getenv('R_USER'), '.Renviron'))
````
After this change, everything is working.

All the best,
V.

parts:
Thanks for sharing these solutions, Beth and Veronica.

There is also a "dir" argument to compileNimble that can change where files are put. If you use `dir = '.'`, it should put files in your working directory (represented in file systems by "."). This could create quite a mess, but at least you would see where things are. There may be cases where the dir argument giving other locations creates its own pains. Let us know if so.

Perry
On Wed, Jan 3, 2024 at 8:29 AM Veronica Winter <veronic...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Chris, Perry, and Beth,

Thank you all for the help trouble shooting this! The issue turned out to be where my temp files were being created. For others who may be experiencing this, my solution was:
```
# change temp file location
write("TMP = 'C:/Users/veron/AppData/Local/Temp'", file=file.path(Sys.getenv('R_USER'), '.Renviron'))
````
After this change, everything is working.

All the best,
V. 
On Tuesday, January 2, 2024 at 6:30:05 PM UTC-5 Beth Gardner wrote:
Hi Chris and Perry,

This was very helpful, I've been beating my head against the wall all day with the same error as Veronica but also with a note about Rtools before above the "Cannot create directory error".  
I don't know why this is happening but when I looked at  Sys.getenv(), the BINPREF was set to an old Rtools folder (maybe I did something wrong at installation?). I looked at my other computer where nimble was working fine (using Rtools4.2) and saw it was not listed so I set it using: Sys.setenv(BINPREF=""), now Rcpp and nimble are working.    

I uninstalled previous R versions and Rtools and then installed R4.3.2 and Rtools 4.3.  Just sharing in case this is helpful to others!

Cheers,
Beth

On Tuesday, January 2, 2024 at 3:14:38 PM UTC-8 Perry de Valpine wrote:
For point 3, specifically, following one of the Rcpp vignettes, you can do:

install.packages("Rcpp")
library("Rcpp") 
evalCpp("2 + 2")

If this does not work, that would indicate that there is a problem in your R and/or Rtools setup that likely has nothing to do with nimble.

Perry



On Tue, Jan 2, 2024 at 2:57 PM Chris Paciorek <paci...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
Hmm, I don't know what is going on. I'm not sure what temporary file it is trying to create or why it seems to be trying to use "C:\\Program Files" but then losing "Program" and putting in a carriage 
return. 

A few thoughts:

1) You might look at the other environment variables (`Sys.getenv()`) and see if that gives any clues. 
2) If you run `tempdir()` in R does it reference a standard location for temporary files?
3) Could you try and run a basic Rcpp example to see if this has anything to do with Nimble?

-chris
